title: Financial Sector Update for 02/07/2018: CG,AINV,GS,AAPL
text:
C +0.56% 
USB +0.99% 
Financial stocks were mostly higher Wednesday, with the NYSE Financial Sector Index rising almost 0.8% while financial companies in the S&P 500 Index were climbing nearly 1.3%. The Philadelphia Housing Sector Index also was almost 1.6% higher. 
In economic news: 
Mortgage applications reversed course again last week, rising 0.7% over prior-week levels that showed a 2.6% decline in the number of homebuyers seeking financing or refinancing their home, according to statistics compiled by the Mortgage Bankers Association. On a seasonally adjusted basis, however, applications were little changed during the seven days ended Feb. 2. Refinancings were down 1.4 percentage points to 46.4% of last week's mortgage activity, its lowest level since July 2017. 
Among financial stocks moving on news: 
+ The Carlyle Group ( CG ) gained Wednesday, rising nearly 5% to an intra-day high of $25.50 a share, after the private-equity investors reported Q4 financial results exceeding analyst estimates. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $1.01 per adjusted unit during the three months ended Dec. 31, up from just $0.02 during the same quarter last year and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.43. Revenue rose 75.4% to $1.01 billion, also topping the $713.3 million Street view. The company declared a $0.33 per share dividend, payable Feb. 27 to shareholder of record on Feb. 20. 
In other sector news: 
+ Apollo Investment ( AINV ) was higher Wednesday, rising over 3% to a session high of $5.59 a share, with the fixed-income and debt investor overcoming fiscal Q3 revenue trailing analyst estimates. Revenue declined 4.8% during the three months ended Dec. 31 from year-ago levels to $64.8 million, missing the Wall Street consensus by $1.1 million. Net investment income also slipped $0.01 from last year to $0.16 per share, matching the Capital IQ consensus. 
+ Goldman Sachs ( GS ) was fractionally higher this afternoon, drifting south from a % advance earlier Wednesday that followed reports the investment banking giant was talking with tech colossus Apple ( AAPL ) about offering financing options to shoppers buying high-end Apple products. For example, buyers of a $1,000 iPhone X could take out a loan from Goldman rather than charging it to credit cards often carrying significantly higher interest rates, the Wall Street Journal said, citing unidentified sources. The talks are ongoing and could yet fall apart, the newspaper said.
